label: copy-phase input token a (from the 3rd copy step on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is the letter a (100% of activation mass has in_tok == a and phase == copy). It never fires on a in the original phase or on the delimiter. It is almost silent when a is fed back at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, about 0.5% of mass); firing rate rises through recall_idx 2-3 and then levels off, so longer sequences and later copy positions contribute most. Remaining false positives are mostly copy-phase a inputs early in short sequences (L 3-6). The strongest activations (near max) are on an a fed back late in the copy, and are often the first of a doubled aa, with the second a weaker. No dependence on output token or digit count was found.

issues: The factual claims check out. All activation mass is in the copy phase with in_tok == a. There is zero activation on a in the original phase or on <DEL>, and in_first == 1 never fires. recall_idx 1 carries 0.5% of mass. Top examples are the first a of a doubled aa, with the second a at about 0.5-0.6 of max.

The onset is graded, not a step, and this accounts for nearly all false positives. Precision of a in the copy phase by recall_idx: r1 about 0 (rising to 0.22 only for L=9), r2 0.30-0.66 (0.43 overall), r3 0.73-0.91, r4+ 0.92-0.98. The r2 false positives occur at every L (L 3-7 precision 0.31-0.48), so 'mostly short sequences' is only partly accurate. Longer L does help a bit at a fixed recall_idx.

Wording: 'from the 3rd copy step on' fits recall_idx >= 2 only if the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) counts as copy step 1. The explanation's own numbering calls recall_idx 1 'the first copy step', which makes recall_idx 2 the 2nd copy step. Also, at recall_idx 2 the feature fires on fewer than half of a inputs, so the label slightly overclaims there.

'No dependence on digit count' is mostly true. Firing rate falls slightly with n_digits (0.011 to 0.006 per step), and prev_tok being a digit lowers precision at r2 (0.28 vs 0.45). These are minor modulations.
No other systematic class was found. prev_tok == a, prev2_tok == a, earlier a counts, out_tok and next_out all give precision about 0.95-0.96 at r >= 4.

Alternative predicates on test: recall_idx >= 3 gives F1 0.895 (mass recall 0.946). recall_idx >= 3 OR (recall_idx == 2 AND L >= 8) gives F1 0.905 (P 0.892, R 0.919, mass recall 0.970). Both are only marginal gains over the original 0.890.
